1	// Parse backticks
2	
3	import type StateInline from './state_inline.ts'
4	
5	export default function backtick (state: StateInline, silent: boolean): boolean {
6	  let pos = state.pos
7	  const ch = state.src.charCodeAt(pos)
8	
9	  if (ch !== 0x60/* ` */) { return false }
10	
11	  const start = pos
12	  pos++
13	  const max = state.posMax
14	
15	  // scan marker length
16	  while (pos < max && state.src.charCodeAt(pos) === 0x60/* ` */) { pos++ }
17	
18	  const marker = state.src.slice(start, pos)
19	  const openerLength = marker.length
20	
21	  if (state.backticksScanned && (state.backticks[openerLength] || 0) <= start) {
22	    if (!silent) state.pending += marker
23	    state.pos += openerLength
24	    return true
25	  }
26	
27	  let matchEnd = pos
28	  let matchStart
29	
30	  // Nothing found in the cache, scan until the end of the line (or until marker is found)
31	  while ((matchStart = state.src.indexOf('`', matchEnd)) !== -1) {
32	    matchEnd = matchStart + 1
33	
34	    // scan marker length
35	    while (matchEnd < max && state.src.charCodeAt(matchEnd) === 0x60/* ` */) { matchEnd++ }
36	
37	    const closerLength = matchEnd - matchStart
38	
39	    if (closerLength === openerLength) {
40	      // Found matching closer length.
41	      if (!silent) {
42	        const token = state.push('code_inline', 'code', 0)
43	        token.markup = marker
44	        token.content = state.src.slice(pos, matchStart)
45	          .replace(/\n/g, ' ')
46	          .replace(/^ (.+) $/, '$1')
47	      }
48	      state.pos = matchEnd
49	      return true
50	    }
51	
52	    // Some different length found, put it in cache as upper limit of where closer can be found
53	    state.backticks[closerLength] = matchStart
54	  }
55	
56	  // Scanned through the end, didn't find anything
57	  state.backticksScanned = true
58	
59	  if (!silent) state.pending += marker
60	  state.pos += openerLength
61	  return true
62	}

content.text:
I fixed it, and `[foo `bar` baz``, `![alt `code` x`` and `[`a`b`` now match the CommonMark output. The markdown-it and CommonMark spec test suites both pass. I couldn't run eslint or the type-check because those commands were denied permission. **Cause:** the bug was in `src/rules_inline/backticks.ts`. To avoid rescanning the line, the backticks rule keeps a cache: the position of the last closing backtick run of each length it has seen, plus a flag saying the whole line has been scanned. The link rule first scans the `[...` label ahead of time to look for the `]`. During that scan, `` `bar` `` was matched as a code span, but the rule never recorded where that closing backtick was. It only recorded closers whose length differed from the opener. The trailing lone `` ` `` then scanned to the end of the line, found nothing, and set the "scanned" flag. When no `]` turned up, the text was parsed again from `[` onwards. At that point the cache said there was no closing backtick after the first `` `bar `` backtick, so the code span came out as literal text. **Fix:** - The rule now records every closing run it sees, matched or not. - It only ever moves a cached position forward, never back. Otherwise a second scan starting earlier in the line could overwrite a later position with an earlier one and wrongly rule out a closer that does exist. I added a test for the three inputs from the report to `test/fixtures/markdown-it/commonmark_extras.txt`. The report says the `zero` preset is affected too, but `zero` has inline code turned off entirely, so `

[foo `bar` baz`

` is the correct output there and I left it alone. The `default` and `commonmark` presets are fixed.
